هِبْرِيَةٌ (S, K) and ↓ هُبَارِيَةٌ (TA) [Scurf on the head;] what is in the hair of the head, resembling bran; (S;) the dirt of the head, that clings to the lower part of the hair, resembling bran; (K;) as also إِبْرِيَةٌ (TA) and تِبْرِيَةٌ. (AO, S, K, in art. تبر.) ―
-b2- Also, [both ↓ words,] What flies about, of, or from, feathers, (K, TA,) and the like: (TA:) and the former, what flies about, of, or from, the down of cotton: (K:) or the fine down that flies about from cotton: (L:) and what becomes scattered about, and compacted, of, or from, canes, or reeds, and the بَرْدِىّ [or papyrus]: (Yaakoob:) pl. of the former, هِبْرِيَاتٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
